rationale:
Issue #163 (label 'bug') reports that ROHD emits illegal SystemVerilog of the form ({a_b_joined,a_shrunk,a_range,a_rsliced,a_plus_b})[3:0], i.e. a bit slice applied to an in-lined expression. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in BusSubset that stops marking the intermediate signal name as unpreferred (_original = 'original_' + bus.name), which forces an explicit named signal instead of allowing the sliced operand to be in-lined as an expression; the added comment states exactly that rationale. The trigger patch is the unchanged upstream test portion of the same single-commit PR #164: it adds expression_bit_select <= [aBJoined, aShrunk, aRange, aRSliced, aPlusB].swizzle().slice(3, 0) plus a SimCompare/iverilog vector, reproducing the reported pattern with pre-existing APIs (swizzle, slice, addOutput, SimCompare) and no API introduced by the fix. The broader set of 10 reproduced selectors is consistent with the same root cause: all simcompare tests in bus_test.dart elaborate the shared BusTestModule, so the illegal generated SystemVerilog for the new output breaks iverilog compilation for every vector in that group; strict evidence confirms buggy full-suite failures are confined to those reproduced triggers and that all fixed isolated/suite/reversed runs pass. No production-side refactor, formatting-only, feature, doc, or config change is present; the only test-file edits are the trigger itself and the required signalToWidthMap entry. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so intel/rohd#163 is not a duplicate, and it matches allowed_root_cause_ids.

Issue #163 (labeled bug) reports that ROHD emits illegal SystemVerilog of the form ({a_b_joined,a_shrunk,a_range,a_rsliced,a_plus_b})[3:0], i.e. a bit slice applied to an inlined expression. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in lib/src/modules/bus.dart that stops marking the BusSubset intermediate signal as unpreferred (_original = 'original_' + bus.name), which forces the expression to be materialized into a named signal before slicing; the added comment states exactly that rationale. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test portion of the same single-commit PR #164: it adds expression_bit_select <= [...].swizzle().slice(3, 0) and a SimCompare.iverilogVector check, using only pre-existing APIs (slice, swizzle, SimCompare) — the fix introduces no new production API, so the trigger cannot depend on one. The broader set of 10 declared selectors all live in test/bus_test.dart and share the BusTestModule fixture, so once the illegal slice-on-expression output is present in the generated module every simcompare test in that suite fails on the buggy revision for the same root cause; strict evidence confirms buggy_differential with at least one selector failing alone, deterministic fingerprints (12 groups), fixed_clean, and full-suite green on the fixed revision for both original and post-minimization runs. Patch touches no test-only, docs, config, or formatting concerns beyond the explanatory comment attached to the changed line. Registry of active same-project root causes is empty, so no duplicate; intel/rohd#163 is the verified allowed key.

risks: The defect is a code-generation correctness bug detected through iverilog compilation, so the trigger's sensitivity depends on the external simulator's strictness; a more permissive simulator could mask a partially incomplete fix.

Nine of the ten declared triggers are pre-existing tests that fail only as collateral of the shared BusTestModule now containing the illegal construct, so they do not independently characterize the defect; only 'simcompare expression bit select' targets it directly.

The fix relies on ROHD's naming-preference mechanics to prevent in-lining rather than an explicit guard in the SystemVerilog emitter, so future changes to name preference handling could silently regress the behavior.
